items.zh: 十一切處 · 階位 · 修證

zh: 次釋十一切遍處法門。十一切處者：一、青；二、黃；三、赤；四、白；五、地；六、水；七、火；八、風；九、空；十、識。此十通名一切處者，一一色各照十方遍滿，故名一切處，乃至空亦如是。前背捨、勝處雖有八色，所照既狹，未能普遍，是以不得受一切之名。復次，經中有時說為「十一切入」。有人解言：「此猶是一切處之異名。」今則不爾，初名以一色遍照十方，名一切處，後心轉善巧，能於一切遍照色中一一互得相入，無相妨閡，故處立一切入名。今明十一切處，即為二意：一、明階位；二、辯修證。
en: Next, explaining the dharma-gate of the ten totalities. The ten totalities are: first, blue-green; second, yellow; third, red; fourth, white; fifth, earth; sixth, water; seventh, fire; eighth, wind; ninth, space; tenth, consciousness. These ten are, in general, named totalities because each and every color illuminates and pervades all ten directions completely — hence they are named totalities, and space, too, follows this same pattern. The eight colors given earlier, within detachment and the stations of mastery, though present, illuminate only a narrow scope, not yet able to pervade everywhere — hence they do not receive the name of totality.

Furthermore, the sutras, at times, speak of these as the "ten totality-entries." Some explain this as merely another name for the totalities themselves. Here, this is not so: the earlier name, taking a single color pervading and illuminating the ten directions, is named a totality; the later mind, growing yet more skillful, is able, within every pervasively illuminating color, to mutually enter one into another without any hindrance whatsoever — hence this stage is given the name totality-entry.
Explaining the ten totalities now has two senses: first, clarifying their stages; second, distinguishing their cultivation and realization.

zh: 第一、明階位者，十一切處，初八色一切處位在第四禪中，次第九空一切處位在空處，第十識一切處位在識處。所以前三禪中不立一切處者，行者初學彼三地中有覺觀喜樂動故，不能令色遍滿停住。上無所有處定，無物可廣，亦不得快樂，佛亦不說無所有處無量無邊，故不立一切處；非有想非無想處心鈍，難取想廣大，故不立一切處。
en: First, clarifying their stages: among the ten totalities, the first eight color-totalities are placed within the fourth dhyāna; next, the ninth, the totality of space, is placed at the sphere of space; and the tenth, the totality of consciousness, is placed at the sphere of consciousness. As for why no totality is established within the first three dhyānas: the practitioner, newly learning within these three stages, still has initial thought, sustained reflection, joy, and happiness moving about, and is thus unable to make color pervade completely and rest unmoving there. As for the sphere of nothingness above, there being nothing there to extend, nor any happiness to be obtained, and the Buddha, moreover, never speaking of the sphere of nothingness as boundless or infinite, no totality is established there either; and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the mind too dull, finding it difficult to grasp any broad, extended perception, no totality is established there either.

zh: 第二、次明修證。行者住第四禪中，以成就自在勝色，爾時應用念清淨心，捨七種色，直念青色，取少青光焰相，如草葉大，一心緣中，即與少青相應。觀心運此少青遍照十方，即見光明隨心普照，一切世間皆見青相遍滿，停住不動，如青世界，是名青一切處。餘七一切處修觀之相亦當如是一一分別。自有師言：「修一切處，緣取草葉等相，因外色起相，遍滿普照。」如此說者，非唯乖失觀門之法，亦與《摩訶衍》所說都不相關。
en: Second, next clarifying cultivation and realization: the practitioner, abiding within the fourth dhyāna, having already accomplished mastery's own superior colors, should, at this time, use the pure mind of mindfulness, setting aside the other seven colors, and hold in mind blue-green alone, taking up a small mark of blue-green light, the size of a blade of grass, the mind fixed one-pointedly upon this object, thereupon corresponding with this small blue-green mark. The contemplating mind then extends this small blue-green mark, illuminating the ten directions completely — one thereupon sees this light, following the mind, illuminating everywhere, the whole world seen entirely filled with the mark of blue-green, resting there unmoving, like a world made entirely of blue-green — this is named the totality of blue-green. The remaining seven totalities' own contemplative mark should each, in turn, be distinguished in this same way.

There is a certain master who says: "Cultivating the totalities means taking up the mark of a blade of grass and the like as one's object, the mark arising by way of external color, and pervading and illuminating everywhere." Explained in this way, this not only strays from and loses the very method of this contemplative gate, but also has nothing whatsoever to do with what is explained in the Mahāyāna treatise.

zh: 行者既已成就，以一切處欲入虛空一切處，當入虛空背捨，但背捨緣狹，未名一切處，今更廣緣十方虛空，故名虛空一切處。欲入識一切處者，當亦先入識處背捨，於識定中廣觀此識，遍滿十方，皆見是識，故名識一切處。行者若欲修一切入，既得一切處成，當以一切處為本，然後用善巧觀心，於青一切中，令黃、赤、白等皆入其中，不壞青之本相，而能於青色之中具見餘色。是則略說一切處、一切入竟。
en: The practitioner, already having accomplished these totalities, wishing to enter the totality of space by way of the totalities themselves, should enter the detachment of the sphere of space; it is only that detachment's own object is narrow, and does not yet receive the name of totality — here, one further broadens the object to the space of the ten directions, hence this is named the totality of space. Wishing to enter the totality of consciousness, one should likewise first enter the detachment of the sphere of consciousness, and, within the concentration on consciousness, broadly contemplate this very consciousness, pervading and filling the ten directions, seeing everything, entirely, as consciousness — hence this is named the totality of consciousness.

Should the practitioner wish to cultivate the totality-entries, having already accomplished the totalities themselves, one should take the totalities as the basis, and then, using a skillful contemplating mind, within the totality of blue-green, cause yellow, red, white, and the rest to each enter within it as well, without destroying blue-green's own original mark, and yet able, within the color blue-green, to see every other color present in full. This, then, briefly explains the totalities and the totality-entries, and brings them to a close.

zh: 問曰：何故不於一切處中分別趣道之相？答曰：一切聲聞經中多說一切處是有漏緣，但是修通法，既於發無漏義劣，故不分別。若依摩訶衍義欲分別者，類如前背捨、勝處中說。今菩薩為欲令神通普徧成就普現色，具足一切法界中事，故修是一切處，故《大品經》亦說名一切處波羅蜜。
en: Question: why is the mark of how the totalities lead toward the path not separately distinguished here? Answer: throughout the śrāvaka scriptures, the totalities are, for the most part, explained as a contaminated object, serving merely as a method for cultivating supernormal powers — being, then, of lesser significance for giving rise to the undefiled, this is not separately distinguished here. Should one wish to distinguish this according to the sense of the Mahāyāna treatise, it follows the same pattern already given above, within detachment and the stations of mastery. Here, the bodhisattva, wishing to cause supernormal powers to pervade everywhere and to accomplish the manifestation of every form completely, becoming complete with every matter throughout the whole dharma-realm, thereby cultivates these very totalities — hence the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, too, speaks of this as the totality-pāramitā.

The totalities complete the arc from the eight forms of detachment's own narrow object through the stations of mastery's own controlled expansion to this final stage's true saturation — a single blade-of-grass-sized fragment of color, deliberately expanded until it fills the visualized world entirely, unmoving. The distinction between a "totality" (one color filling everything) and a "totality-entry" (multiple colors interpenetrating within a single totality without destroying each other's own mark) is a subtle but important refinement, and the treatise is careful to flag the wrong way to teach it — starting from an external object like an actual blade of grass, rather than from the mind's own cultivated image — as a real error some other master had made, not just a hypothetical one. The totalities are also the one dharma-gate in this whole three-part observational sequence (detachment, mastery, totality) explicitly not given its own "approach to the path" treatment, on the grounds that śrāvaka tradition treats it as useful chiefly for supernormal powers rather than liberation directly — though the Mahāyāna reading, as usual in this treatise, reclaims it anyway.

options: blue, yellow, red, white, earth, water, fire, wind, space, consciousness
quiz.why: The ten are blue, yellow, red, white, earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; the last two are not colors.

quiz.q: Detachment and mastery have the eight colors; why are they not called totalities?
options: their light is narrow and not yet pervasive
quiz.why: Each totality-color pervades the ten directions; the earlier colors illuminated only narrowly, so they are not called totalities.

options: one color pervading is totality; colors mutually entering one another is totality-entry
quiz.why: One color pervading the ten directions is a totality; when the mind grows skillful and the pervading colors interpenetrate without obstruction, it is a totality-entry.

quiz.q: Where are the totalities placed, and why none in the first three dhyānas?
options: colors in the fourth, space and consciousness in their spheres; the first three are moved by thought, joy, happiness
quiz.why: The eight colors are in the fourth dhyāna, space in the sphere of space, consciousness in that sphere; the first three dhyānas, stirred by thought, joy, and happiness, cannot hold the color still and pervading.

quiz.q: From what mark does the blue totality begin, and what view is criticized?
options: one takes a small blue light the size of a grass blade and extends it; the view of taking an external grass blade is rejected
quiz.why: One takes a small blue light, the size of a grass blade, and extends it everywhere. The view that one takes an actual external grass blade is said to miss the method entirely.
